title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 343 (Company Liquidator to exercise certain powers subject to sanction)

content.overview: The Company Liquidator may, with the sanction of the Tribunal when the company is being wound up by the Tribunal: (i) pay any class of creditors in full; (ii) make any compromise or arrangement with creditors or persons claiming to be creditors (present or future, certain or contingent); or (iii) compromise any call, debt, liability or claim between the company and a contributory or other debtor, and all questions relating to assets, liabilities or the winding up, on agreed terms, take security and give a complete discharge. Creditors or contributories may apply to the Tribunal regarding any exercise or proposed exercise of these powers.
content.glance: Liquidator needs Tribunal sanction to pay a class of creditors in full or to compromise claims/calls/debts; creditors/contributories may challenge.
content.study: Section 343 restricts certain significant powers of the Company Liquidator in a Tribunal winding up to those exercised with Tribunal sanction: paying any class of creditors in full; making compromises or arrangements with creditors or claimants; and compromising calls, debts, liabilities and claims with contributories or other debtors, including giving complete discharges and taking security. The Central Government may by rules permit exercise of some compromise powers without sanction in prescribed circumstances. Any creditor or contributory may apply to the Tribunal with respect to any exercise or proposed exercise of these powers, and the Tribunal may pass such orders as it thinks fit after hearing the applicant and the Liquidator.

sections.heading: Powers requiring sanction
sections.body: Pay class of creditors in full; compromise/arrangement with creditors; compromise calls/debts/claims with contributories or debtors.

sections.heading: Challenge
sections.body: Creditor or contributory may apply to Tribunal regarding exercise or proposed exercise of the powers.

provisions.title: Company Liquidator to exercise certain powers subject to sanction

examples.title: Compromise of claim
examples.body: The Company Liquidator proposes to settle a disputed debt at 40% without litigation. He must obtain Tribunal sanction under s. 343 before binding the estate.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Liquidator pay preferential creditors in full without sanction?
hypotheticals.analysis: Paying any class of creditors in full requires Tribunal sanction under s. 343(1)(i). Preferential ranking itself is governed by ss. 326–327.

rows.left: Company Liquidator to exercise certain powers subject to sanction

misconceptions.trap: The Liquidator has unfettered power to compromise all claims.
misconceptions.correction: Compromises and full payment of a class of creditors require Tribunal sanction (subject to any rules under sub-section (2)).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 343 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the rule of s. 343. II. Apply to facts. III. Conclude.
